method.review: A separate agent audited the eight priority-three proposals; root reconciled wording and added independently opened AT&S English support. This is collaborative research review, not blinded outcome adjudication.
method.validation_limits: Existing per-decision structural validation can check clean fields, HTTPS URLs, sorted evidence and cutoff bounds, but does not verify semantic truth or external source bytes.

population.selection: All 13 priority-one and all 10 priority-two leads; eight priority-three leads selected for semiconductor-substrate versus PCB boundaries and the two co-addressed GlobalFoundries records. This is not random or recall-representative.

basis: docs/methodology.md Objective and scope and facility examples
scope_interpretation.historical_identity: Old names, addresses and certificates can establish historical scope, not continued production at the last EEA reporting year or today. Shared addresses do not authorize source-ID, entity or building merges.
scope_interpretation.inclusion: Historical semiconductor-device fabrication and semiconductor-materials/substrate activities at the source-reported facility, including compound semiconductors. This is broader than the AI-critical cohort.
scope_interpretation.ordinary_pcb_and_pcba: Proposed exclusions are reviewer operational judgments based on affirmative board-manufacturing descriptions. The normative contract does not contain a verbatim universal PCB exclusion. PCB, rigid-flex and IMS products do not themselves establish IC-substrate or semiconductor-device assembly/test activity.
scope_interpretation.unresolved_boundaries: Equipment-only activity remains unresolved. Semiconductor wafer reclaim may fit materials scope when exact-facility process evidence is established. Neither LED nor photovoltaic labels alone settle device-fabrication versus downstream-assembly scope.
